submissions.findingTextShort: A branded mnemoPQQ randomized trial reported selected cognitive-domain signals, but the source has a published correction and strong commercial provenance.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled parallel-group trial tested mnemoPQQ at 21.5 mg/day for 12 weeks in healthy adults and reported selected cognitive-domain improvements. PubMed links a published correction notice to this article, and multiple authors were affiliated with the commercial supplier. Any use of the trial must preserve branded formulation, population, regimen, sponsor provenance, and its correction/erratum relationship rather than promoting the uncorrected publication as generic PQQ evidence.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy middle-aged/older adults in a branded-product randomized trial.
submissions.usageContext: mnemoPQQ branded PQQ disodium-salt product, 21.5 mg/day for 12 weeks.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Selected-domain findings, modest sample size, commercial provenance and a linked correction constrain generalization. Draft-only pending source governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 35917215 is the published correction to PMID 34415830 and must remain linked before that RCT is admitted or promoted.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PubMed identifies PMID 35917215 / DOI 10.1080/27697061.2022.2099711 as a published correction for the mnemoPQQ cognition trial PMID 34415830. Source admission and downstream claim construction should therefore carry an explicit correction/erratum relationship so the canonical evidence graph cannot treat the original paper as an independent uncorrected source or ignore known corrected metadata/content.
submissions.usageContext: Bibliographic correction-lineage provenance only; not an efficacy result.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The correction should be inspected during source attestation for the exact amended content before clinical promotion.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 20 mg/day PQQ disodium-salt trial reported age-stratified cognitive signals, with manufacturer-affiliated authors and outcome timing differing by age group.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A double-blind placebo-controlled study administered PQQ disodium salt at 20 mg/day for 12 weeks to adults aged 20–65. Reported cognitive signals differed by age stratum and assessment timing, with younger adults showing selected processing/flexibility changes earlier and older adults showing selected memory changes later. Authors were affiliated with Mitsubishi Gas Chemical Company, so age subgroup, commercial provenance and formulation identity must remain attached rather than collapsing the study into a universal cognition claim.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy adults aged 20–65 with age-stratified analyses.
submissions.usageContext: PQQ disodium salt, 20 mg/day for 12 weeks.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Age-stratified findings and manufacturer affiliation constrain broad inference. Draft-only pending registry and semantic attestation.

submissions.findingTextShort: A small BioPQQ randomized trial reported selected attention/working-memory signals in older healthy adults and should remain branded/formulation specific.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized placebo-controlled double-blind trial in 41 older healthy participants administered BioPQQ at 20 mg/day for 12 weeks and reported selected Stroop/attention and visuospatial cognitive changes. The modest sample and branded-product identity limit the finding to preliminary formulation-specific cognition evidence rather than a class-wide PQQ efficacy conclusion.
submissions.usageContext: BioPQQ branded PQQ disodium salt, 20 mg/day for 12 weeks.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small trial and selective cognitive outcomes require replication. Draft-only pending governance.

submissions.findingTextShort: EFSA concluded BioPQQ was safe under the specified intended conditions up to the proposed 20 mg/day for healthy adults excluding pregnant/lactating women; this is a safety scope, not efficacy evidence.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The EFSA novel-food opinion evaluated PQQ disodium salt marketed as BioPQQ for food-supplement use in healthy adults, excluding pregnant and lactating women, at a maximum proposed 20 mg/day. EFSA concluded the novel food was safe under those specified intended conditions. This authoritative receipt may support that bounded regulatory safety context only; it does not prove cognitive efficacy, safety above the reviewed exposure, safety in excluded populations, or equivalence among every commercial PQQ preparation.
submissions.populationContext: EFSA intended-use safety evaluation for healthy adults excluding pregnant/lactating women.
submissions.usageContext: BioPQQ/PQQ disodium salt, proposed maximum 20 mg/day under the evaluated intended use.
submissions.safetyContext: Regulatory novel-food safety scope; not clinical efficacy and not a universal no-risk threshold.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Human ADME data were limited in the EFSA assessment, and the conclusion is formulation/intended-use specific. Draft-only pending governed authoritative-source registration.

submissions.findingTextShort: The live zero-source PQQ profile embeds EFSA-specific 20 mg/day and pregnancy/lactation safety language without an attached canonical receipt.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The current PQQ profile exposes sourceCount zero and an empty claim map while its contraindication text refers specifically to EFSA's 20 mg/day reviewed level and pregnancy/lactation exclusion. Study- or authority-specific safety facts should not appear as durable public derived truth without the matching canonical authority receipt and scope metadata. The profile should remain NOINDEX/needs-review until evidence and safety provenance reconcile.
submissions.usageContext: Repository evidence-receipt/provenance finding; no public safety mutation in this fragment.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This finding does not invalidate the EFSA conclusion; it documents the missing canonical linkage needed to audit the public statement.
